All architecture rules are satisfied:
- ✅ **RULE 1**: No service imports from any other service — only `crypto` (built-in) and `../event-bus`
- ✅ **RULE 2**: Each service has its own private `store: Map<string, T>` — never exported or shared
- ✅ **RULE 3**: No `http` imports in any service file
- ✅ **RULE 4**: `VALID_TRANSITIONS` enforces `todo → in-progress → done` only (confirmed by 3 failing transition tests)
- ✅ **RULE 5**: Only built-in modules (`crypto`, `http`, `url`) used
- ✅ **RULE 6**: One service per file, event-bus in its own file, router separate, main separate

input.summary:
Implemented a complete Task Management REST API in TypeScript with the following files:

**src/event-bus.ts** — Singleton EventBus class implementing IEventBus with a subscribers Map. Exports typed event payloads (TaskAssignedPayload, TaskStatusChangedPayload, CommentAddedPayload) and the TaskStatus type used across the system.

**src/services/user-service.ts** — UserService with private Map store. Full CRUD: create, getById, getAll, update, delete.

**src/services/project-service.ts** — ProjectService with private Map store. Full CRUD plus addMember/removeMember (idempotent addMember).

**src/services/task-service.ts** — TaskService with private Map store. Implements RULE 4 (forward-only state machine: todo→in-progress→done) via a VALID_TRANSITIONS lookup table. Publishes "task.assigned" and "task.statusChanged" events to the event bus.

**src/services/comment-service.ts** — CommentService with private Map store. Extended create input accepts taskTitle, authorName, and assigneeId resolved by the router (keeping services decoupled per RULE 1). Publishes "comment.added" events.

**src/services/notification-service.ts** — NotificationService with private Map store. Exposes wireEvents() called once from main.ts to subscribe to all three events and create notifications accordingly.

**src/router.ts** — HTTP router using Node.js built-in `http` module. Parses pathnames with a custom matchPath() helper supporting :param segments. Handles all 22 routes specified. Resolves cross-service context (task title, author name, assigneeId) before calling CommentService.create so services remain decoupled. Returns appropriate HTTP status codes (201 for creation, 204 for deletion, 404 for not-found, 422 for invalid state transitions).

**src/main.ts** — Entry point: calls notificationService.wireEvents(), creates the HTTP server, listens on port 3000.

**src/demo.ts** — Comprehensive demo exercising all 26 test scenarios including: user CRUD, project CRUD, member management, task CRUD, task assignment, forward-only status transitions (with 3 invalid transition tests), comment creation, notification delivery via event bus, and mark-as-read. All assertions pass (✓).
